algorithm: Maintain, for every noble, its number of friends with a larger label. The survivors of the complete elimination process are exactly nobles whose count is zero. Each edge changes only the count of its smaller endpoint, and the answer changes only when that count crosses zero.
correctness_argument: For an edge u<v, v cannot be killed while u is alive because u is a weaker friend. A noble with no higher friend can therefore never be vulnerable: while it has friends they are weaker, and otherwise it is isolated. Inducting over increasing labels, every noble with a higher friend eventually loses all its lower friends; those lower friends have this noble as a higher friend and die first. Its higher friend is still alive, so the noble is then killed. Thus zero higher-degree is exactly the survivor predicate.
edge_cases: An edgeless graph leaves all n nobles alive.
Removing the last higher friend restores one survivor.
problem_understanding: Prove that every noble with a higher friend is eliminated before that friend.
